predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Eyalet of Tunis, which the Husainid bey took over from the Ottoman province

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: Tunisia, a French protectorate from 12 May 1881

ledger.x: July 1705: Husayn bin Ali seizes power at Tunis and founds the Husainid beylik.
1794: a strip on the Tripolitanian frontier passes to Tunis.
24 April 1881: French troops enter Tunisia from the north.
12 May 1881: the Treaty of Bardo ends the independent beylik.

wars.name: Algerian intervention in Tunis (1756)
wars.outcome: Ali I was overthrown by two sons of his predecessor, who 'took Tunis with help from the governor of Constantine'; Muhammad I ar-Rashid reigned from 22 September 1756.

wars.name: Tripolitanian civil war
wars.outcome: Burghul seized Tripoli on 29-30 July 1793 and 'occupied Djerba, an island under Tunisian jurisdiction, on 30 September 1794'; on 19 January 1795 the Karamanlis retook Tripoli with the aid of the Bey of Tunis.

wars.name: Hammouda's war with Algiers (1807)
wars.outcome: 'Hammouda I's forces ended Algerian attempts to overthrow the beys' in 1807; no territory changed hands on the page.

wars.name: French invasion of Tunisia (1881)
wars.outcome: The French entered from the north on 24 April and landed at Bizerte from 1 May 1881; the Treaty of Bardo (12 May) made Tunisia a protectorate; the Sfax rising (27 June) was put down on 16 July, Gabes retaken on 30 July, Kairouan on 26 October, and Tunis…

certainty.note: The pages give no treaty frontier: the Algerian frontier is mentioned but not described, the Tripolitanian frontier is not on the pages, and the Saharan south is 'ill-defined'; the northern and coastal limits are firmer than the desert.
